title: Half of Japanese Households Unprepared for Disasters
paragraphs: Japan is one of the most earthquake-prone countries in the world, yet recent surveys suggest that many households there are still not ready for a major disaster.

In a survey carried out in July 2026 by Taiko Pharmaceutical, a company based in Osaka, 1,095 people in their twenties to sixties were asked about the emergency supplies they had at home. Around 76% said they had stored drinking water, 67% had emergency food and 63% had flashlights. However, only 41% had emergency toilet bags, which can be used when toilets cannot be flushed after an earthquake. Furthermore, more than half of all respondents did not have enough toilet bags for even one person. Experts recommend about 35 bags per person, which would last around a week.

This is a serious problem, because 66% of respondents said that not being able to use the toilet was their biggest concern after a disaster, even more than food or water. Only 54% knew that they should not flush toilets after a major earthquake, because damaged pipes can cause sewage to leak.

Other surveys show similar results. In a July 2026 survey of 3,413 adults by the house builder Ichijo Komuten, about 60% said they had not prepared for earthquakes, and more than half of them said they did not know what to do. Meanwhile, in a survey by the Japanese Red Cross Society, 69% admitted that they had taken no measures or insufficient measures to prepare for a disaster as large as the 2011 earthquake and tsunami.

The Japanese government is trying to change this. On November 2, 2026, a new National Disaster Management Agency was launched. The agency asked households to store at least three days' worth of food and water, and a week's worth if possible, as well as portable toilets. The government estimates that there is a 70% chance of a major earthquake hitting Tokyo within the next 30 years.
